subject: communication-studies
intro: Communication studies is the theory behind the message economy: its graduates get paid to craft, analyse and research how organisations, media and people persuade and inform each other.

roles.title: Public Relations Specialists
roles.what: Promote or create an intended public image for individuals, groups or organisations, writing and selecting material for release across communications media, with many specialists focusing on social media.
roles.where: The rhetoric and persuasion unit's ethos, pathos and logos is the theory under every pitch, the media and cultural studies unit's framing and agenda setting explains what earns coverage, and the research methods unit backs evaluation.

roles.title: Writers and Authors
roles.what: Originate and prepare written material such as scripts, stories, advertisements and other content, shaping ideas into forms that inform, persuade or entertain their audiences.
roles.where: Semiotics and meaning-making from communication theory, argument structure from the rhetoric unit, and the audience and effects research in media studies give writers the models for choosing what to say and to whom.

roles.title: Editors
roles.what: Plan, coordinate, revise and edit written material, reviewing proposals and drafts for publication and steering content decisions from idea to print.
roles.where: The medium-and-message topic in communication theory and the audience research in media and cultural studies train the judgement editors apply to what a piece is for, while discourse analysis sharpens line-level revision.

roles.title: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
roles.what: Research local, regional, national and online market conditions, gathering information on potential sales, competitors, prices and marketing methods, and analysing web metrics to raise visibility with target markets.
roles.where: The research methods unit is the direct toolkit — quantitative surveys and experiments, qualitative discourse and ethnography, and research ethics — while framing and audience effects from media studies guide how findings become campaigns.

roles.title: Communications Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach university courses in communications such as organisational communication, public relations, broadcasting and journalism, combining teaching with research on how humans communicate.
roles.where: Every unit of this syllabus maps to a lecture course — theory, rhetoric, interpersonal and organisational communication, media studies — and the research methods unit is the training ground for the published scholarship the career demands.
